class.name: Treasure Hunter (LotR)
class.proficiency: Dexterity, Intelligence, Acrobatics, Athletics, Deception, Insight, Investigation, History, Perception, Persuasion, Survival, Sleight of Hand, Stealth
class.tools: A tool of your choice among cartographer's tools, a gaming set, or thieves' tools

trait.name: Treasure Hunter
trait.text:
Far over the Misty Mountains cold, To dungeons deep and caverns old. We must away ere break of day, To seek the pale enchanted gold.
The world has seen the passing of the glory of many Dwarven kings and Elven lords, and their heritage is now buried in Orc-infested dungeons. Hoards of stolen gold and jewels, guarded by fell beasts, beckon all who dare to find them. You seek to recover what is lost, even when it means braving unspeakable dangers.
Source: The Lord of the Rings p. 57

feature.name: Starting Treasure Huter
feature.text:
As a 1st-level Treasure Hunter, you begin play with 8 + your Constitution modifier hit points.
You are proficient with the following items, in addition to any proficiencies provided by your race or background.
• Armor: light armor • Weapons: simple weapons, shortswords, swords • Tools: A tool of your choice among cartographer's tools, a gaming set, or thieves' tools • Skills: Choose 4 from Acrobatics, Athletics, Deception, Insight, Investigation, Old Lore, Perception, Persuasion, Riddle, Sleight of Hand, Stealth, and Travel
You begin play with the following equipment, in addition to any equipment provided by your background.
• Leather shirt, any simple melee weapon, and thieves' tools • (a) a short sword or (b) a sword • (a) a bow and a quiver of 20 arrows or (b) any simple melee weapon
If you forgo this starting equipment, as well as the items offered by your background, you start with 4d4 × 10 gp to buy your equipment.
Source: The Lord of the Rings p. 57

feature.name: Multiclass Treasure Hunter
feature.text:
If your group uses the optional rule on multiclassing in the Player's Handbook, here's what you need to know if you choose treasure hunter as one of your classes.
Ability Score Minimum: As a multiclass character, you must have at least the following ability score(s) to take a level in this class, or to take a level in another class if you are already a treasure hunter.
• Dexterity 13
Proficiencies Gained: When you gain your first level in a class other than your initial class, you gain only some of your new class's starting proficiencies, here are the proficiencies you gain when you take your first level as a treasure hunter.
• Armor: light armor • Weapons: simple weapons • Tools: thieves' tools • Skills: Choose 1 from Acrobatics, Athletics, Deception, Insight, Investigation, Old Lore, Perception, Persuasion, Riddle, Sleight of Hand, Stealth, and Travel
Source: The Lord of the Rings p. 67

feature.name: Shadow Path
feature.text:
Dragon-Sickness: Adventurers who find themselves on the Road to seek lost riches run the risk of catching the age-old disease capable of turning a pile of enchanted gold into bitter ashes. As the Shadow tightens its grip on their hearts, the world shrinks around them and their closely guarded possessions.
Source: The Lord of the Rings p. 58

feature.name: Expertise
feature.text:
At 1st level, choose any combination of two of your skill and tool proficiencies. Your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make that uses either of the chosen proficiencies. At 9th level, you can choose another two proficiencies (in skills or with tools) to gain this benefit.
Source: The Lord of the Rings p. 58

feature.name: Sneak Attack
feature.text:
Beginning at 1st level, you know how to strike subtly and exploit a foe's distraction. Once per turn, you can deal an extra 1d6 damage to one creature you hit with an attack if you have advantage on the attack roll. The attack must use a finesse or a ranged weapon. You don't need advantage on the attack roll if another enemy of the target is within 5 feet of it, that enemy isn't incapacitated, and you don't have disadvantage on the attack roll. The amount of the extra damage increases as you gain levels in this calling, as shown in the Sneak Attack column of the Treasure Hunter table.
Treasure Hunter 1 | 1d6 2 | 1d6 3 | 2d6 4 | 2d6 5 | 3d6 6 | 3d6 7 | 4d6 8 | 4d6 9 | 5d6 10 | 5d6
Source: The Lord of the Rings p. 58

feature.name: Cunning Action
feature.text:
Starting at 2nd level, you can take a bonus action on each of your turns in combat. This action can be used only to take the Dash, Disengage, or Hide action.
Source: The Lord of the Rings p. 58

feature.name: Treasure Hunter Speciality
feature.text:
Treasure can take different forms — from wondrous objects in a Dragon-hoard, to precious information stolen from the Enemy.
When you reach 3rd level, you choose a speciality to pattern your career as a Treasure Hunter after. You can choose to be a Burglar or a Spy.
Source: The Lord of the Rings p. 58

feature.name: Virtue
feature.text:
At 4th level, and again at 6th and 8th level, you can take a common or cultural virtue of your choice. You can take each virtue only once. As normal, you cannot increase an ability score above 20 using this feature. At 6th level, instead of taking a virtue you can gain a craft slot and a craft of your choice from the Scholar's Crafts list.
Source: The Lord of the Rings p. 59

feature.name: Uncanny Dodge
feature.text:
Beginning at 5th level, when an attacker that you can see hits you with an attack, you can use your reaction to halve the attack's damage against you.
Source: The Lord of the Rings p. 59

feature.name: Virtue Improvement
feature.text:
At 6th level, you can take a common or cultural virtue of your choice. You can take each virtue only once. As normal, you cannot increase an ability score above 20 using this feature. At 6th level, instead of taking a virtue you can gain a craft slot and a craft of your choice from the Scholar's Crafts list.
Source: The Lord of the Rings p. 59

feature.name: Virtue Improvement
feature.text:
At 8th level, you can take a common or cultural virtue of your choice. You can take each virtue only once. As normal, you cannot increase an ability score above 20 using this feature.
Source: The Lord of the Rings p. 59

feature.name: Expertise Improvement
feature.text:
At 9th level, choose two of your skill or tool proficiencies. Your proficiency bonus is doubled for any ability check you make that uses either of the chosen proficiencies.
Source: The Lord of the Rings p. 58

feature.name: Reliable Talent
feature.text:
By 10th level, you have refined your chosen skills until they approach perfection. Whenever you make an ability check that lets you add your proficiency bonus, you can treat a d20 roll of 9 or lower as a 10.
Source: The Lord of the Rings p. 59

feature.name: Specialty: Burglar
feature.text:
Burglar wants a good job, plenty of Excitement and reasonable Reward, that's how it is usually read.
Yours are the venerable arts of pickpocketing, lock picking, or otherwise getting hold of the possessions of others and accessing protected areas.
Source: The Lord of the Rings p. 59

feature.name: Clever-Handed (Burglar)
feature.text:
Starting at 3d level, you can use the bonus action granted by your Cunning Action to make a Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check or take the Use an Object action.
Source: The Lord of the Rings p. 59

feature.name: Tree-Climber (Burglar)
feature.text:
Also at 3rd level, you gain the ability to climb faster than normal; climbing no longer costs you extra movement. In addition, you can add your Dexterity modifier to Strength (Athletics) checks you make to climb or jump, and to the distance you cover (in feet) when you make a running jump.
Source: The Lord of the Rings p. 59

feature.name: Quiet-Footed (Burglar)
feature.text:
Starting at 7th level, you have advantage on Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) and Dexterity (Stealth) checks if you move no more than half your speed on the same turn.
Source: The Lord of the Rings p. 59

feature.name: Specialty: Spy
feature.text:
But it appeared that he was nobody's friend, and nobody could recollect when he had joined their party.
The Enemy sends many agents among the Free Peoples, and you intend to spy upon them, lest they undermine your efforts to resist the Shadow.
Source: The Lord of the Rings p. 59

feature.name: Cunning Eye (Spy)
feature.text:
Starting at 3rd level, you can add your Intelligence modifier to your Wisdom (Insight) and Wisdom (Perception) checks. In addition, you can use the bonus action granted by your Cunning Action to take the Search action.
Source: The Lord of the Rings p. 59

feature.name: Weak Spot (Spy)
feature.text:
Also at 3rd level, you can use a bonus action to make an Intelligence (Investigation) or Wisdom (Perception) check against a creature within 30 feet of you that you can see, contested by the target's Dexterity (Stealth) check. If you win the contest, you can use your Sneak Attack against that target even if you don't have advantage on the attack roll, but not if you have disadvantage on it. This benefit lasts for 1 minute or until you successfully use this feature against a different target.
Source: The Lord of the Rings p. 59

feature.name: Sharp-Eyed (Spy)
feature.text:
Starting at 7th level, you have advantage on Intelligence (Investigation) and Wisdom (Perception) checks if you move no more than half your speed on the same turn.
Source: The Lord of the Rings p. 59
